sub: Named after the burūj, the great stars, in ayah 1
theme: Comfort for persecuted believers and a warning to their persecutors. Stay firm like the people of the trench: Allah sees everything, His grip is severe, and His word is protected.
story: Revealed in Makkah when persecution was at its peak. The Quraysh were using force and torture to turn new Muslims away from Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ told of a boy sent to learn sorcery who chose faith instead. He could only be killed “in the name of Allah, Lord of the boy.” When he died the crowd believed, so the king dug trenches of fire for them.

The surah curses those persecutors, promises Paradise to the steadfast, reminds the Quraysh that stronger armies were destroyed, and ends by saying the Quran they deny is preserved and cannot be changed.

sections.title: Cursed are the trench-diggers who burned believers only for their faith
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the sky with its great stars, the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed. Cursed are the people of the trench, who sat by a blazing fire watching believers burn. Their only complaint against them was faith in Allah, who owns everything and sees everything.
points: By the starry sky, the promised Day, witness and witnessed
Cursed are the people of the trench of fuelled fire
They sat by it, watching what they did to believers
Their only grudge: the believers’ faith in Allah
He owns the heavens and earth and witnesses all
sections.matters: It gives persecuted believers a model: people who chose fire over giving up their faith. And it reminds persecutors that what they punish is exactly what Allah praises, and He is watching.
sections.story: Reportedly this happened in Najrān in Yemen, under a king called Dhū Nuwās, about seventy years before the Prophet ﷺ; other reports mention trenches elsewhere. A mother hesitated at the edge, and her baby said: “Be patient, mother, you are on the truth.”
explained: The oaths: the sky with its burūj, great stars; the Promised Day, the Day of Judgement; and shāhid and mashhūd, in one report Friday and the Day of ʿArafah, with other views too. Then: qutila aṣḥāb al-ukhdūd, cursed are the people of the trench.

They dug trenches, filled them with fire and fuel, and sat on the edges watching as believers who refused to give up their faith were thrown in. They had nothing against them except that they believed in Allah, al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd, who owns the heavens and earth and witnesses everything.
teaches: Faith can be worth more than life itself.
Persecution for belief is never hidden from Allah.
Oppressors may watch and enjoy it now; Allah is watching them.
Believing in Allah is never a crime.
sections.hook: Witness words run through it: shāhid and mashhūd (3), shuhūd (7), shahīd (9). The section opens with the sky (1) and closes with the heavens and earth (9).

sections.title: Hell for unrepentant persecutors, gardens for believers; Allah is severe yet Loving
sections.meaning: Those who persecuted believers and never repented get Hell and the burning punishment. Believers who did good get gardens with rivers, the great success. Allah’s grip is severe; He begins creation and repeats it; He forgives and loves; He owns the glorious Throne and does whatever He wills.
points: Persecutors who don’t repent: Hell and burning
Believers who do good: gardens with rivers, the great success
Your Lord’s grip is severe; He begins and repeats
Forgiving, Loving, Lord of the Throne, doing what He wills
sections.matters: Even after describing such cruelty, the door of repentance stays open. The section pairs severity with forgiveness and love, so the oppressor fears and the believer hopes.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues from the people of the trench and speaks to the persecutors in Makkah.
explained: Fatanū: they tortured, here by burning. Those who did it to believing men and women and then did not repent get Hell and ʿadhāb al-ḥarīq, the burning. Notice “then did not repent”: even people who burned Allah’s friends are invited to repent. Believers who did good get gardens with rivers, al-fawz al-kabīr.

Allah’s baṭsh, His seizing grip on wrongdoers, is severe. He starts creation and brings it back. Yet He is al-Ghafūr, forgiving whoever repents, and al-Wadūd, the Loving. He owns the mighty Throne, al-Majīd, and does whatever He intends. Nothing can stop Him.
teaches: No sin is too great for repentance while there is time.
Real success is Paradise, not winning in this world.
Fear His grip and hope in His love together.
Allah does what He wills; no plan can block Him.
sections.hook: Ayat 10 and 11 both begin inna alladhīna: persecutors, then believers. Then a run of Allah’s names and attributes: al-Ghafūr, al-Wadūd, dhū al-ʿArsh, al-Majīd, faʿʿāl (14–16).

sections.title: Pharaoh and Thamūd destroyed; deniers are surrounded, the Quran is preserved
sections.meaning: Has the story of the armies reached you, Pharaoh and Thamūd? They were destroyed. Yet the disbelievers keep denying, while Allah surrounds them. And this is a glorious Quran, kept safe in the Preserved Tablet.
points: The armies of Pharaoh and Thamūd
The deniers keep denying; Allah surrounds them
A glorious Quran in a Preserved Tablet
sections.matters: The Makkan leaders trusted their numbers. This section reminds them of stronger armies that were destroyed, and tells them the Quran they reject can’t be defeated or changed.
sections.story: No specific incident. It warns the Quraysh, who were persecuting Muslims and calling the Quran poetry and fortune-telling.
explained: Al-junūd, the armies: Pharaoh with his forces, and Thamūd. Both denied their messengers and were destroyed, and no army could protect them. Their story proves ayah 12: your Lord’s grip is severe.

Still, the disbelievers stay stuck in denial. But Allah is behind them and all around them: they cannot escape His knowledge or His power. And what they deny is a Qurʾān majīd, glorious and rich in meaning, in al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ, guarded from any change, addition or loss.
teaches: Power and numbers didn’t save Pharaoh; they won’t save anyone.
No one escapes Allah’s knowledge or power.
Denying the Quran cannot change it; Allah guards it.
sections.hook: Majīd appears twice: in 15 (al-Majīd) and in 21 (Qurʾān majīd). The surah opens with the sky of stars (1) and ends with the Preserved Tablet (22).

groups.text: By the sky of great stars, the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed.
Cursed are the people of the trench, who sat by its fire watching what they did to believers.
Their only grudge was the believers’ faith in Allah, who owns and witnesses everything.
Persecutors who don’t repent get Hell’s burning; believers who do good get gardens, the great success.
Your Lord’s grip is severe. He begins creation and brings it back.
He is Forgiving and Loving, Owner of the glorious Throne, doing whatever He wills.
Has the story reached you of the armies of Pharaoh and Thamūd?
The disbelievers keep denying, but Allah surrounds them from behind.
This is a glorious Quran, in a Preserved Tablet.

1.explain: Burūj: the great stars; others say the stations the sun and moon pass through. Allah swears by the sky that holds them, a sign of His power.

2.explain: Al-yawm al-mawʿūd: the Day of Judgement, the Day Allah promised to gather everyone, first and last. He never breaks His promise.

3.explain: Shāhid and mashhūd: the witness and the witnessed. A report from the Prophet ﷺ names Friday and the Day of ʿArafah. Many other meanings are given.

4.explain: Qutila: cursed and destroyed. Ukhdūd: a long ditch dug in the ground. The persecutors dug trenches to burn believers.
4.why: Reportedly revealed about Dhū Nuwās, a king in Yemen, who dug trenches at Najrān and burned the believers who refused to give up their faith.

5.explain: The trench held a fire dhāt al-waqūd, packed with fuel to keep it blazing.

6.explain: They sat around it on its edges, reportedly on chairs, to watch.

7.explain: Shuhūd: present and watching what they did to the believers. One report says the believers’ souls were taken before the fire touched them, and the fire rose and burned the watchers.

8.explain: Naqamū: resented. Their only “crime” was believing in Allah, al-ʿAzīz, the Mighty, al-Ḥamīd, the Praiseworthy: a quality worth praise, not punishment.

9.explain: He owns the heavens and the earth and witnesses everything. Did the persecutors not fear that the true Owner was watching them?

10.explain: Fatanū: tortured and burned. “Then did not repent”: the door of repentance was open even to them. Their punishment is Hell and burning, matching their deed; some say it burned them in this world too.

11.explain: Believers in the heart who act with their limbs get gardens with rivers flowing beneath. Al-fawz al-kabīr: the great success, Allah’s pleasure and His home of honour.

12.explain: Baṭsh: a violent seizing. When your Lord seizes wrongdoers, His grip is severe.

13.explain: Yubdiʾu wa yuʿīd: He begins creation and brings it back after death. No one shares this with Him.

14.explain: Al-Ghafūr forgives every sin of those who repent. Al-Wadūd: the Loving, and the Loved. Pairing the two shows He forgives repenting sinners and loves them too.

15.explain: Dhū al-ʿArsh: Owner of the mighty Throne above all creation. Al-Majīd is read two ways: describing Allah, the Glorious, or the Throne. Both meanings are correct.

16.explain: Faʿʿāl li-mā yurīd: whatever He wants, He does, and no one can oppose it. Created beings need help to do what they want; Allah needs none.

17.explain: Has the story reached you of al-junūd, the armies that gathered against the prophets?

18.explain: Pharaoh, with his forces, and Thamūd. They denied their messengers and Allah destroyed them, a warning to those denying the Prophet ﷺ.

19.explain: Rather, the disbelievers of your people stay stuck in denial of you and the Quran, and learn nothing from those before them.

20.explain: Allah is behind them, surrounding them with knowledge and power. They cannot escape Him.

21.explain: Qurʾān majīd: glorious and noble, full of good and knowledge. It is not poetry or fortune-telling, as they claimed.

22.explain: In al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ, the Preserved Tablet, guarded from change, addition, loss and devils. One reading makes “preserved” describe the Quran itself.
